title: I Put the Church Potluck Allergen Card Where Everyone Could See

parts.text: I set my labeled tray on the potluck table and found someone had peeled the sesame sticker off. I am twenty-six, kitchen-table designer energy, church volunteer by habit. The fellowship hall smelled like coffee urns and wet coats. My friend Nadia cannot do sesame. I had written SESAME - NADIA'S in tape. The tape was in the trash, sticky side still shiny. Pastor Glen's wife, Ruth, was arranging rolls. "It looked ugly," she said. "People know." I said, "People don't." Nadia was in the bathroom. A kid reached for the noodles. I blocked the tray. Ruth laughed. "Don't make this medical." It was medical. My notes app had the last three potlucks where unlabeled sauce made Nadia leave early. I photographed the trash tape and the tray. Glen appeared with a ladle. "What's the holdup?" Ruth said I was creating fear. I said I was creating a label. The tape dispenser on the counter was empty because Ruth had used the last of it on a sign that said JOY. JOY was not an ingredient. Nadia came back, saw my face, saw the tray. "Did it happen again?" she asked, quiet. Before I could answer, a deacon named Paul announced the buffet was open, and a line formed that would hit the sesame noodles in about twelve seconds.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The buffet line is twelve seconds from unlabeled sesame, and the only tape is in the trash.

social.video_title: She peeled the sesame label for aesthetics — Part 1/2
social.description: Coffee-urn church hall, JOY tape on a sign, medical tape in the trash. The line was already moving. Would you have blocked the tray?

parts.text: I picked up the tray and took it back to the kitchen. Paul said, "That's not sharing." I said, "Sharing without a label is gambling." Nadia stood beside me. Ruth called it drama. Glen looked at the trash tape photo on my phone, then at JOY. He is not brave, but he is not stupid. He delayed the line with a prayer that lasted long enough for me to retape with masking tape from the janitor closet, the kind that smells like dust. I wrote SESAME in letters you could see from the coffee urn. Ruth did not speak to me for a month. Nadia ate. Nobody died, which is a low bar that still matters. The next potluck, Glen announced a label rule like it had been his theology all along. I brought extra tape. Paul asked if I was satisfied. I said satisfaction is a weird word for not sending a friend to the ER. Ruth eventually apologized in a card with a cross on it and no mention of sesame. I keep the card in a drawer with rubber bands. I still volunteer. I still check trash cans for peeled stickers. That is my spiritual practice now, and it is more useful than JOY in all caps.

social.video_title: Masking tape theology beat the JOY sign — Part 2/2
social.description: I pulled the tray, retaped in dust-smelling masking tape, and ate the low bar of nobody in the ER. Would you have stayed a volunteer?
